hooks.text: A city-killer asteroid missed Earth by just six hours.
How did a 300-meter asteroid miss Earth by six hours unseen?
Six hours is all that saved Earth from a 300-meter asteroid.

title: The Asteroid That Missed Earth by Six Hours
description: In 1989, a 300-meter asteroid crossed Earth's orbital path just six hours after our planet left, and astronomers didn't see it coming.

beats.text: A city-killer asteroid missed Earth by just six hours.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a near-Earth asteroid flying past Earth, 2019

beats.text: We assume global networks would spot space hazards approaching days in advance.
beats.visual: Astronomical survey star field at Palomar Observatory, 1989

beats.text: But on March 22, 1989, the 300-meter asteroid Asclepius crossed our orbital path completely unseen.
beats.visual: Diagram of Earth crossing asteroid orbit, 1989

beats.text: Astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas only discovered it nine days after it had already swept past.
beats.visual: Samuel Oschin telescope at Palomar Observatory, California, 1989

beats.text: The rock crossed through the exact spot Earth occupied six hours earlier, at 684,000 kilometers away.
beats.visual: Earth and Moon scale distance diagram, 1989
queries: orbit of the Moon around Earth diagram

beats.text: Geophysicists estimated a direct hit would have unleashed energy comparable to a 600-megaton atomic bomb.
beats.visual: NASA asteroid impact crater simulation illustration, 2019

beats.text: Here is the part I can't get past: nobody knew a regional disaster was looming.
This terrifying blind spot launched modern planetary defense programs to track every incoming city-killer asteroid.
